mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) and Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals increased household investment and liquidity, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than six months in a low-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for > 6 months AND CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) to below 3.5% while nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) growth accelerates above 250,000 signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% AND PAYEMS > 250000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for four consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which reduces corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
